title: Growth Incremental Analysis of Thin Sections from Marine Molluscs
author: Niklas Hausmann
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.67chhiw

steps.title: Section oyster shells
steps.instruction: Using a Buehler ISOMET 1000 precision saw with a Series 15LC Diamond Wafering Blade (No. 11‑4276), cut the oyster shell at the hinge in the direction of growth; optionally make a second cut to remove excess shell length.

steps.title: Prepare plastic moulds
steps.instruction: Clean cylindrical plastic moulds with ethanol, let dry for 5 minutes, then coat the interior with Buehler Release Agent (Catalog #20‑8185‑016) and dry for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Embed shells in epoxy
steps.instruction: Place the sectioned shells face‑down in 1‑ or 2‑inch moulds (size chosen by hinge length), add a mixture of Buehler Epoxy Resin (Catalog #20‑8140‑12B) and Epoxy Hardener (Catalog #20‑8142‑016) at a 2 : 1 volume ratio, and cure at constant humidity and temperature overnight (≈12 h).

steps.title: Grind and polish block
steps.instruction: After curing, remove the resin block from the mould and sequentially grind the hinge surface on a Buehler Motorpol 2000 using metallographic grit papers P600, then P1200, then P2500. Rinse the surfaces with water, polish with a cloth and Buehler 3 µm polycrystalline suspension (Catalog #40‑6016), then let dry overnight (≈12 h).

substeps.instruction: Polish using 3 µm polycrystalline suspension on a polishing cloth.

steps.title: Bond block to glass slide
steps.instruction: Attach the polished facet of the resin block to a glass slide using Loctite 322 UV‑curable adhesive, expose to a UV light source, and allow to harden for 24 hours.

steps.title: Trim block to hinge slice
steps.instruction: With the sample bonded to the slide, cut away the bulk of the resin block using the Buehler ISOMET 1000 saw, leaving an embedded hinge slice 200–500 µm thick on the slide.

steps.title: Final fine grinding
steps.instruction: Repeat the grinding sequence (step 4) on the remaining hinge slice to lightly grind shell and resin until a final thin section of approximately 50 µm thickness is obtained.
